events.title: Critical Atlassian Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Read Known Files Across 8 Products
events.summary: A critical flaw in eight Atlassian Data Center products allows unauthenticated attackers to read specific files in the web application root if they already know the exact file name and path.
events.why_it_matters: The vulnerability has a CVSS score of 9.3, indicating a high severity risk. It enables attackers to read sensitive files without authentication, potentially exposing confidential data and facilitating further attacks.
events.resolution: A critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-21589, affected eight Atlassian Data Center products, letting unauthenticated attackers read known files in the web application root. Exploitation began within hours of proof-of-concept publication, and SANS honeypots logged scans from DigitalOcean-hosted IP addresses. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 15 October 2026. The incident is now resolved.

claims.text: CISA lists CVE-2026-21589 as exploited in the wild, added 2026-10-15, with US federal agencies due to fix it by 2026-10-18.
CVE-2026-21589 is rated 9.3 (critical) under CVSS 4.0 by the CNA that assigned it.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2026-21589 being exploited in the next 30 days at 4.3%.
17 independent sources report this event.
